newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt court convicts reporter in Sadat widow case.
newsitem.headline: Egypt court convicts reporter in Sadat widow case.

text.p: An Egyptian court on Monday gave a one-year suspended sentence to an opposition newspaper reporter for forging a birth certificate that said he fathered a child with the widow of the late president Anwar Sadat.

The court in Cairo said Ahmed Fikry Abdel-Hamid of al-Ahrar newspaper was guilty of libel when he wrote a story last August headlined "Jihan Sadat has an illegitimate child" based on the ease with which official documents could be forged in Egypt.
Abdel-Hamid paid registry clerk Gamal Zaki Garas 20 pounds ($6) to issue him a birth certificate that named Abdel-Hamid as the father and Sadat's widow Jihan as the mother.
The criminal court also found Abdel-Hamid guilty of invading and abusing the privacy of the Sadat family and of bribing a state employee.
The clerk, Garas, was cleared of forgery charges while Mostafa Bakry, the editor of the paper at the time, was acquitted of libel charges.
The newspaper is the mouthpiece of the opposition Ahrar party. The party's leader Mostafa Kamel Murad fired Bakry after the public outcry that followed the article's publication.
